can you squash the change ?

I thought I'd separate it because it is in packet-ssh.c.

According to what @jmayer2 told me for the last Merge Request, it is better to have functionally coherent small changes. So what I intended to do is not to have 2 versions of packet-sftp.c (because I add it from scratch, so I can as well remove the spaces up front). And have 2 versions of packet-ssh.c, the first one with the code changes to activate the sub dissector, and a second one just correcting the white space and super fast and easy to review.  
That was my intent anyway, but maybe I failed to do it. Or do you think it is better to have fewer versions of the file, even if it means more diffs per version?

Please tell me if you still want me to squash the change.

Having them separate for the review process is good, it makes the change much easier to review. In this particular case however, it doesn't, as it's a new file anyway so the whitespace changes don't make it harder to find the changes to the code.

In general, i.e. not in this particular case, whether to squash them during merge is a question of "philosophy" and Wireshark is not nearly as strict as e.g. the Linux kernel is and which I personally prefer.

The good thing about gitlab is, that in the merge request (somewhere down) is a small tickbox that says to squash the individual patches. Just tick it and you should be good.

Based on my own experience (verified several times) the Gitlab automatic squash is lost when the Wireshark Gitlab Utility performs the automatic rebase to ensure a linear history. Please instead perform the squash manually before the merge.

> as it's a new file anyway so the whitespace changes don't make it harder to find the changes to the code.

Sorry if I wasn't clear before, but I modify one file (packet-ssh.c) and I add one file (packet-sftp.c). So for the new file I did amend the commit, but for the existing one I kept the versions separate.

Anyway, please complete the review and I'll squash the commits (or should I do the squashing before the review? BUT BY ALL MEANS DO THE REVIEW PLEASE ;o)  [I still have some changes to push in following Merge Requests]
